selected_skill.purpose: Guide the agent toward a single-API reference page workflow that pulls behavior details from source, tests, and local example pages.

selection_rationale: High-star match for API reference drafting with explicit guidance on examples, tables, behavior notes, and version history.
Public repository inputs only. No external account, login state, publish permission, or user data access is required.
Supports a single-container task where with_skill and without_skill can differ only by environment/skills.

rejected_high_star_skills.reason: Broader markdown editing workflow with weaker pressure toward a single API reference page.
Tutorial flow is adjacent, but the task target is an API reference page.
Optimized for drift audits across docs trees rather than authoring one missing API page.

task_shape.runtime: single-container Python workspace with bundled repository snapshots and local MDX references
task_shape.solver_action: complete a missing API page and manifest instead of emitting an analysis report

planned_verifier_focus: Formal build entrypoint produces the required MDX page and manifest
Section order, tables, examples, and version history match the contract
API behaviors are grounded in bundled source, tests, readme, and release inputs
Manifest stays aligned with documented API items and example identifiers
Alternate fixture reruns prove the build is not hardcoded to one visible snapshot

real_data_sources.reference: PQueue options and task options for v8.1.1
GitHub release page for p-queue v8.1.1

with_without_difference_policy: Only environment/skills/ and the corresponding runtime skill-copy logic may differ between with_skill and without_skill variants.

local_validation.buggy_workspace_expected_result: Fails substantive verifier checks because the starter build emits only a partial page and a partial manifest.

iteration_notes: Do not rely on editing the bundled skill contents to complete the task.
Do not alter instruction.md, tests, data, dependencies, or contracts between with_skill and without_skill variants.
Favor action-level failures such as missing API coverage or unsupported behavior statements over cosmetic markdown differences.
Finalize README metrics only after completed E2B comparison runs.
